pages.page_summary: This page contains exercises 5.1 through 5.3 for a Physics chapter. Exercise 5.1 asks to determine the sign of work done in various scenarios. Exercise 5.2 involves calculating work done by applied force, friction, and net force for a body moving on a rough surface. Exercise 5.3 refers to Figure 5.11, which displays four different potential energy functions V(x) in one dimension, asking students to identify forbidden regions and minimum total energy.
knowledge_points: Exercise 5.1: Determine the sign (positive or negative) of work done in five specific physical scenarios: (a) lifting a bucket, (b) gravitational force on the bucket, (c) friction on a body sliding down an incline, (d) applied force on a body moving with uniform velocity on a rough plane, (e) resistive force of air on a vibrating pendulum.

Exercise 5.2: A 2 kg body initially at rest moves under a 7 N horizontal force on a table with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.1. Calculate work done by applied force, friction, and net force in 10 s, and the change in kinetic energy.

Exercise 5.3: Analyze potential energy functions V(x) shown in Fig. 5.11. Identify regions where a particle with total energy E (indicated by a cross) cannot be found, and determine the minimum total energy required for the particle to exist in each case.

embedded_text.visual_description: Top-left graph in Fig. 5.11 showing a step potential.
Top-right graph in Fig. 5.11 showing a staircase potential.
Bottom-left graph in Fig. 5.11 showing a potential well.
Bottom-right graph in Fig. 5.11 showing a symmetric potential well with curved sides.

visuals.description: A set of four potential energy function graphs labeled Fig. 5.11. The top-left graph shows a step function where V(x) is 0 for x < a and V0 for x > a. The top-right graph shows a staircase function with levels V0, V3, and intermediate steps. The bottom-left graph shows a rectangular potential well with depth -V1 between x=a and x=b, and height V0 outside. The bottom-right graph shows a symmetric potential well with curved sides, depth -V1, and width defined by -b/2 and b/2.
visuals.educational_role: Illustrates different one-dimensional potential energy landscapes to test understanding of classical mechanics constraints on particle motion.
